lead_headline: Restaurant tracker logs 4 fresh leads (2 openings, 2 closures) as China BBQ debuts Westminster and Colfax and Cream expands to Pearl Street, while foreclosure filings drop 17% week-over-week

restaurant.blurb: 4 new leads today (2 openings, 2 closures) lift inventory to 79 active cases (39 openings, 40 closures)—Wednesday's haul matches Tuesday's pace as April tracking begins. Fresh openings: China BBQ plants flag at 3041 W 92nd Ave Westminster (confidence 7, replaces Tasty Express in rotation-heavy address); Colfax and Cream flags Pearl Street expansion (confidence 8, third location since May 2024 Broadway launch). Union Station corridor now carries 9 active opening leads vs 8 closures, maintaining downtown's net-positive tilt as suburbs hemorrhage fast-casual flags (Dairy Queen Westminster, Fort Logan closures accumulate). April's opening two days post +6 net leads (+1.5/day) vs March's +0.7 daily average—early signal of seasonal acceleration or database catch-up noise pending week's close.

foreclosure.blurb: 35 filings this week mark 17% decline from prior week's 42 with zero properties breaching $2M threshold—top case caps at $686K Arapahoe County (24296 E Ohio Drive) as 105 auctions queue for next 7 days.

liquor.blurb: Zero applications today—April 2 extends statewide filing blackout to 33 consecutive days, eclipsing December 2024's 12-day record by 175%. Databaselag theory solidifies: no social chatter, no regulatory announcements, suggesting 50-70 application backlog awaiting system restoration. If Friday delivers third straight zero, escalate to Liquor Enforcement Division—12,316-case archive shows no precedent for month-long void during non-holiday periods.

reputation.blurb: 1 mention yesterday caps March's exit at 65 weekly citations (+23% vs prior week's 53)—April 2 opens with Instagram self-promo post as sole pickup while Denver Post, Hoodline maintain week's dominance (13, 6 mentions respectively). Social platforms (Instagram, Facebook, x.com) command 49% weekly share vs traditional media's 29%, sustaining March's platform inversion. Rolling 30-day average settles at 56 mentions/week as April resets—watch for quarterly pattern shift if business/CRE desk pickups cool post-Q1 earnings cycle.

subscriptions.blurb: Net +1 yesterday (2 new, 1 canceled) pushes MTD to +1 (+1.0/day) as April opens on neutral footing—90-day net holds +133 despite March's zero-net stumble. Two-day April start matches March's opening rhythm (2 new/day), but churn risk persists: past 7 days post +14 net (26 new, 12 canceled) vs prior week's +24 (33 new, 9 canceled), marking 42% acquisition slowdown and 33% churn acceleration. Longer view: YTD +132 (+1.5/day) still outpaces MTD's +1.0 flat open, but March's first monthly zero since November 2025 flags momentum crack. Critical week ahead: if April 1-7 matches last week's +14 pace, quarter escapes March's stall; sub-+10 weekly net signals structural deceleration requiring intervention.
